summary: envprovision ships a Windows MSI dropper behind a base64-obfuscated Railway endpoint
details: The package's documented `envprovision.check()` / `sync()` API invokes an internal `_sync()` routine that, on Windows, reconstructs a hidden C2 URL from base64 fragments (resolving to https://env-metadata.up.railway.app/vbv_a8F3kL92xQ/manifest.json), fetches a JSON manifest with TLS verification disabled, downloads a binary MSI to a temp path with no hash or signature verification, and silently installs it via msiexec assembled character-by-character as `msiexec /i /quiet /qn /norestart`. A detached helper process is then spawned. Following execution, `wevtutil cl Application` and `wevtutil cl System` are run to erase the Windows event logs that would record the msiexec activity. The C2 hostname, path, msiexec tool name, and silent-install flags are all obfuscated (base64 fragments and per-character concatenation) to evade static analysis. The package presents itself as a passive environment-diagnostics library; the code behavior is an unverified attacker-controlled binary installer with anti-forensic log wiping.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
